concise_answer: The original code was preserved, and Plan C/Plan D reconstruct the evaluation around available artifacts; no exact paper-number reproduction is claimed.
Datasets, candidate evaluation, utility metrics, and neural baselines were reconstructed or extended using local processed artifacts.
D5E-D5K local LLM work uses a 20-user ML-1M diagnostic subset and should not be described as full paper LLM reproduction.

topic: Why is the LLM part not exact reproduction?
concise_answer: It does not run all seven paper LLMs, closed-source APIs, full user counts, or repeated paper experiments; some exact models are retired or hardware/API blocked.

topic: Why are hallucination and candidate validity important?
concise_answer: D5E showed valid JSON can still contain non-candidate IDs, so HR/NDCG alone miss reliability failures.
D5G strict candidate-ID-only prompting improved Qwen2 utility and candidate validity in the diagnostic subset.

topic: What did candidate position bias show?
concise_answer: D5F showed that reordering the same candidates changed utility and reliability, so candidate order is a robustness factor.

topic: What did Qwen vs Mistral show?
concise_answer: D5I showed Qwen2 strict had higher utility than local Mistral strict in this subset while both achieved perfect candidate validity.
D5J showed local LLM re-ranking did not improve the candidate-order reference and reliability differed by model.

topic: What did history length sensitivity show?
concise_answer: D5K showed history window length changed utility and output stability even under strict prompts with zero hallucination.
Claude 3 Haiku exact is retired, Llama3 70B is blocked locally by hardware, closed APIs need approval/budget, and LastFM lacks valid utility setup.

topic: What is the main contribution of the project?
concise_answer: It turns an incomplete exact reproduction into a transparent reconstructed reproduction plus reliability-focused local LLM diagnostics.
A separate approved phase could recover official artifacts, broaden user counts, add constrained decoding, or run small closed-source API diagnostics with explicit budget.
